The patient reports a temperature of 38.5 last night and chills.

Tonsils are swollen with bilateral white exudate.
Anterior cervical lymph nodes are enlarged and tender.
Ears are normal and lungs are clear.
Rapid strep test is positive.
Strep pharyngitis, supported by fever, tonsillar exudate, tender anterior cervical nodes, absence of cough, and a positive rapid strep test.

statements.text: Amoxicillin was considered but not given because of the patient's history of hives with amoxicillin.
Azithromycin 500 mg once daily for five days was prescribed and sent to the patient's pharmacy.
The patient was advised to finish the full antibiotic course even if feeling better, with improvement expected within two to three days.
The patient may continue ibuprofen for pain and fever, drink plenty of fluids, and use warm salt water gargles.
The patient should stay home from work until on the antibiotic for at least 24 hours and fever-free, and a work note will be provided.
The patient should return or go to the emergency department for trouble breathing, inability to swallow saliva, or inability to fully open the mouth.
The patient should call if not improving within 48 to 72 hours.
